_about: Which NIST AI RMF subcategories each check gives evidence for. Numbers and official wording checked on 16 Oct 2026 against NIST AI 100-1 (AI RMF 1.0, Jan 2023) and NIST AI 600-1 (Generative AI Profile, Jul 2024). 'checks' maps a finding id or a passed-check name to subcategory ids. 'by_severity' adds subcategories to every finding of that severity. 'every_report' lists subcategories that every report gives evidence for; 'showed' is the text shown for them ({target} and {started_at} are filled in). 'gai_risks' are the matching risk names in NIST AI 600-1. To correct the mapping, edit this file only; see README, 'NIST AI RMF'.
source: NIST AI 100-1 (AI RMF 1.0) and NIST AI 600-1 (Generative AI Profile)
disclaimer: This report gives evidence for the data-access parts of the NIST AI RMF; it does not certify compliance. The AI RMF is voluntary guidance and has no certification.

subcategories.label: Keep a list of your AI systems
subcategories.official: Mechanisms are in place to inventory AI systems and are resourced according to organizational risk priorities.

subcategories.label: Have rules for risks from outside suppliers' software
subcategories.official: Policies and procedures are in place that address AI risks associated with third-party entities, including risks of infringement of a third-party's intellectual property or other rights.

subcategories.label: Security: can the AI's access to data be misused
subcategories.official: AI system security and resilience - as identified in the MAP function - are evaluated and documented.

subcategories.label: Accountability: a login, and knowing who asked for what
subcategories.official: Risks associated with transparency and accountability - as identified in the MAP function - are examined and documented.

subcategories.label: Privacy: personal and secret data the AI can reach
subcategories.official: Privacy risk of the AI system - as identified in the MAP function - is examined and documented.

subcategories.label: Plan a response to each high risk
subcategories.official: Responses to the AI risks deemed high priority, as identified by the MAP function, are developed, planned, and documented. Risk response options can include mitigating, transferring, avoiding, or accepting.

subcategories.label: Keep an eye on outside suppliers' software and control it
subcategories.official: AI risks and benefits from third-party resources are regularly monitored, and risk controls are applied and documented.

subcategories.label: Keep checking after go-live
subcategories.official: Post-deployment AI system monitoring plans are implemented, including mechanisms for capturing and evaluating input from users and other relevant AI actors, appeal and override, decommissioning, incident response, recovery, and change management.

every_report.GOVERN 1.6: Records one AI connection to data ({target}) and what it can reach, for your list of AI systems. The wizard's "Found on this computer" lists the others on this machine.
every_report.MANAGE 4.1: A dated check (run at {started_at}) that can be run again the same way to spot changes after go-live.

not_covered.label: Accuracy, bias and model testing
not_covered.showed: This tool only looks at what the AI can reach in your data. It does not test how accurate or fair the AI's answers are, or the model itself. Use other methods for those.
